verdict.headline: High risk: broad non-compete targeting existing products, USD 250,000 liquidated damages, and New York jurisdiction.
summary: The agreement includes an aggressive non-compete clause that directly restricts your core existing agritech products across Southeast Asia.

findings.title: Non-compete clause restricts existing core business
findings.quote: Accordingly, during the term of this Agreement and for a period of three (3) years thereafter, the Counterparty shall not, and shall procure that its affiliates, directors and shareholders shall not, directly or indirectly, engage in, develop, market or invest in any business that competes with any business of the Group anywhere in the Territory, including the design or sale of irrigation controllers, soil sensors or farm analytics software.
findings.why_risky: An NDA should only protect confidential information, not restrict you from running your business. This clause shuts down your ability to sell or develop your own irrigation and agritech products across ASEAN for up to six years.
findings.standard: Standard NDAs contain no non-compete covenants. Any commercial restrictions belong in a definitive commercial agreement and should never restrict existing operations.
findings.suggested_ask: Please remove Section 6 entirely; confidentiality obligations in Section 2 provide adequate protection for discussions.

findings.standard: Parties entering exploratory discussions retain full rights to develop, sell, and market their existing product lines.
findings.suggested_ask: Please delete Section 6.4 in its entirety along with the rest of Section 6.

findings.quote: In addition to any other remedy, the Counterparty shall pay to Halvexa, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, the sum of USD 250,000 for each breach of this Agreement, without any limit on the aggregate amount payable, together with all attorneys' fees and costs incurred by Halvexa in enforcing this Agreement.
findings.why_risky: Pre-set damages of USD 250,000 per breach with no aggregate cap create catastrophic financial liability for technical or minor oversights, and multiplying daily breaches could quickly bankrupt a small enterprise.
findings.standard: Standard NDAs rely on ordinary unliquidated damages where the claimant must prove actual financial loss, alongside injunctive relief.

findings.why_risky: Resolving a dispute under New York law requires retaining US attorneys at exorbitant rates, putting a Malaysian business at a crippling disadvantage in any enforcement action.
findings.standard: Parties in cross-border relationships in this region typically agree to local law or a neutral regional framework such as Singapore law with regional dispute resolution.
